{{Short description|Asymptotic values of Hermite or Laguerre polynomials}}

The '''Plancherel–Rotach asymptotics''' are [[Asymptotic expansion|asymptotic]] results for [[orthogonal polynomials]]. They are named after the [[Switzerland|Swiss]] mathematicians [[Michel Plancherel]] and his [[PhD]] student [[Walter Rotach]], who first derived the asymptotics for the [[Hermite polynomial]] and [[Laguerre polynomial]]. Nowadays asymptotic expansions of this kind for orthogonal polynomials are referred to as ''Plancherel–Rotach asymptotics'' or of ''Plancherel–Rotach type''.<ref>{{cite thesis|title=Reihenentwicklungen einer willkürlichen Funktion nach Hermite'schen und Laguerre'schen Polynomen|first=Walter|last=Rotach|date=1925|doi=10.3929/ethz-a-000092029|publisher=ETH Zurich|hdl=20.500.11850/133495 }}</ref>

The case for the associated Laguerre polynomial was derived by the Swiss mathematician [[Egon Möcklin]], another PhD student of Plancherel and [[George Pólya]] at [[ETH Zurich]].<ref>{{cite thesis|first=Egon|last=Möcklin|title=Asymptotische Entwicklungen der Laguerreschen Polynome|date=1934|publisher=ETH Zurich|doi=10.3929/ethz-a-000092417|hdl=20.500.11850/133650 }}</ref>

== Hermite polynomials ==
Let <math>H_n(x)</math> denote the n-th Hermite polynomial. Let <math>\epsilon</math> and <math>\omega</math> be positive and fixed, then
* for <math>x =(2n+1)^{1/2}\cos \varphi</math> and <math> \epsilon \leq \varphi \leq \pi -\epsilon</math>
::<math>
e^{-x^2/2}H_n(x)
=2^{n/2+1/4}(n!)^{1/2}(\pi n)^{-1/4}(\sin \varphi)^{-1/2}
\bigg\{\sin\left[\left(\tfrac{n}{2}+\tfrac{1}{4}\right)(\sin 2\varphi-2\varphi)+3\tfrac{ \pi}{4}\right]+\mathcal{O}(n^{-1})\bigg\}
</math>
* for <math>x =(2n+1)^{1/2}\cosh \varphi</math> and <math>\epsilon \leq \varphi \leq \omega</math>
::<math>
e^{-x^2/2}H_n(x)
=2^{n/2-3/4}(n!)^{1/2}(\pi n)^{-1/4}(\sinh \varphi)^{-1/2}
\exp\left[\left(\tfrac{n}{2}+\tfrac{1}{4}\right)(2\varphi-\sinh 2\varphi)\right]
\big\{1+\mathcal{O}(n^{-1})\big\}
</math>
* for <math>x =(2n+1)^{1/2}-2^{-1/2}3^{-1/3}n^{-1/6}t</math> and <math>t</math> complex and bounded
::<math>e^{-x^2/2}H_n(x)
=3^{1/3}\pi^{-3/4}2^{n/2+1/4}(n!)^{1/2}n^{-1/12}
\bigg\{A(t)+\mathcal{O}\left(n^{-{2/3}}\right)\bigg\}</math>
where <math>A(t) = 3^{-1/3} \pi \operatorname{Ai}(-3^{-1/3}t)</math> and <math>\operatorname{Ai}</math> denotes the [[Airy function]].<ref name="Szegő">{{cite book|first1=Gábor|last1=Szegő|title=Orthogonal polynomials|volume=4|publisher=American Mathematical Society|place=Providence, Rhode Island|pages=200–201|date=1975|isbn=0-8218-1023-5}}</ref>

== Probabalist's Hermite polynomials ==

Let <math>\operatorname{He}_n(x)</math> denote the n-th [[Hermite_polynomials | probabalist's Hermite polynomial]]. These are related to the (physicist's) Hermite polynomials <math>H_n(x)</math> by the relations <math> H_n(x)=2^\frac{n}{2} \operatorname{He}_n\left(\sqrt{2} \,x\right), \quad \operatorname{He}_n(x)=2^{-\frac{n}{2}} H_n\left(\frac {x}{\sqrt 2} \right).</math>  

[[File:Three approximations to the Hermite polynomials.png|thumb|Three approximations for the probabilists Hermite polynomials illustrated when n=25]]

The Plancherel–Rotach asymptotics for <math>\operatorname{He}_n(x)</math> can be written as<ref name="NicaOrtmann2026">{{cite journal |last1=Nica |first1=Mihai |last2=Ortmann |first2=Janosch |title=A Gaussian integral formula for the Hermite polynomials: Combinatorics, asymptotics and applications |journal=Probability Surveys |volume=23 |publisher=Institute of Mathematical Statistics and Bernoulli Society |pages=255–343 |year=2026 |doi=10.1214/26-PS37}}</ref>:

* [Small <math>x</math> regime] For fixed <math>\alpha\in (0,\pi/2)</math>, set <math>x=2\cos(\alpha)\sqrt{n}</math> and then as <math> n \to \infty </math> one has
<math display="block">
\begin{aligned}
    \operatorname{He}_n \left(x \right) &= 
    \sqrt{\frac{2n^n}{\sin(\alpha)}}
    e^{n(\cos^2\alpha-\frac12)}\,
    \cos\left(n \left(\sin\alpha\cos\alpha -\alpha\right) -\frac 12\left(\alpha+\frac\pi2\right)\right)\left(1+o(1)\right)
\end{aligned}
</math>
 
* [Large x regime] For fixed  <math>\gamma > 0</math>, set <math>x=2\cosh(\gamma)\sqrt{n}</math>. Then as <math> n \to \infty </math> one has <math display="block">
\begin{aligned}
    \operatorname{He}_n \left(x \right) &= 
    n^{n/2}e^{n \left(\gamma+\frac12 e^{-2\gamma}\right)}\, \frac{e^{\gamma/2}}{\sqrt{2\sinh(\gamma)}}
    \left(1+o(1)\right). 
\end{aligned}
</math>

* [Edge regime] For fixed <math>u \in \mathbb{R}</math>, set <math>x = 2\sqrt{n} + n^{-1/6}u</math>. Then as <math> n \to \infty </math> one has
<math display="block">
\begin{aligned}
    \operatorname{He}_n \left(x \right) &= 
    \sqrt{2\pi} e^{n/2} n^{n/2} n^{1/6} e^{un^{1/3}} \operatorname{Ai}(u) \left(1+o(1)\right).
\end{aligned}
</math> 

== (Associated) Laguerre polynomials ==
Let <math>L^{(\alpha )}_n(x)</math> denote the n-th associate Laguerre polynomial. Let <math>\alpha</math> be arbitrary and real, <math>\epsilon</math> and <math>\omega</math> be positive and fixed, then
* for <math>x =(4n+2\alpha + 2)\cos^2\varphi</math> and <math>\epsilon\leq \varphi \leq \tfrac{\pi}{2} -\epsilon n^{-1/2}</math>
::<math>
e^{-x/2}L^{(\alpha )}_n(x)
=(-1)^{n}(\pi \sin \varphi)^{-1/2}x^{-\alpha/2-1/4}n^{\alpha/2-1/4}
\big\{\sin\left[\left(n+\tfrac{\alpha+1}{2}\right)(\sin 2\varphi-2\varphi)+3\pi/4\right] +(nx)^{-1/2}\mathcal{O}(1)\big\}
</math>
* for <math>x =(4n+2\alpha + 2)\cosh^2\varphi</math> and <math>\epsilon\leq \varphi \leq \omega</math>
::<math>
e^{-x/2}L^{(\alpha )}_n(x)
=\tfrac{1}{2}(-1)^{n}(\pi \sinh \varphi )^{-1/2}x^{-\alpha/2-1/4}n^{\alpha /2-1/4}
\exp\left[\left(n+\tfrac{\alpha+1}{2}\right)(2\varphi-\sinh 2\varphi)\right]
\{1+\mathcal{O}\left(n^{-1}\right)\}
</math>
* for <math>x =4n+2\alpha + 2 -2(2n/3)^{1/3}t</math> and <math>t</math> complex and bounded
::<math>e^{-x/2}L^{(\alpha)}_n(x)
=(-1)^n\pi^{-1}2^{-\alpha-1/3}3^{1/3}n^{-1/3}
\bigg\{A(t)+\mathcal{O}\left(n^{-2/3}\right)\bigg\}</math>
where <math>A(t) = \pi \operatorname{Ai}(-3^{-1/3}t)</math> and <math>\operatorname{Ai}</math> denotes the [[Airy function]].<ref name="Szegő">{{cite book|first1=Gábor|last1=Szegő|title=Orthogonal polynomials|volume=4|publisher=American Mathematical Society|place=Providence, Rhode Island|pages=200–201|date=1975|isbn=0-8218-1023-5}}</ref>
